title: Spiders May Sleep in Two Stages
paragraphs: Scientists at the University of Bonn in Germany studied a jumping spider from Australia. It is called Portia fimbriata, and it is about as big as a one-euro coin. People know this spider because it is a clever hunter.

The team put each spider in a small dish and filmed it with special cameras for many days and nights. They also played sounds to see how fast the spiders reacted. This helped them to tell sleep from simple rest.
The spiders had two kinds of sleep. In one kind, they moved their eyes and their legs twitched, like people in dream sleep. However, the scientists say this does not mean that spiders dream.

questions.a: At the University of Bonn in Germany.

questions.q: Why did the team play sounds?
questions.a: To see how fast the spiders reacted and to tell sleep from rest.

questions.q: What happened in the second kind of sleep?
questions.a: The spiders moved their eyes and their legs twitched.
